panels.title: Rate-limit rejections by bucket
panels.description: WHAT: rate of requests refused with HTTP 429 by the RateLimiter plug, split by bucket (auth / upload / social / password_change / public / admin / e2e_helper / global). HOW: rate over stacks_rate_limit_rejected_count_total, emitted at the plug call site with a bounded bucket atom (never request input). MEANS: near-zero in normal operation — most traffic sits well under its per-bucket window. WATCH: a spike on the auth bucket is a credential-stuffing / brute-force signal (cross-check login-failure panels); a spike on public/global is scraping or DoS; a bucket that is throttling legitimate users points to a too-tight limit or a shared-NAT hotspot worth re-sizing.

panels.title: Client-IP resolution by source
panels.description: WHAT: rate at which the rate-limiter resolved the per-IP key from each source (trusted_proxy = Fly edge `fly-client-ip` header / remote_ip = socket peer). HOW: rate over stacks_rate_limit_client_ip_count_total, emitted by RateLimiter.get_ip/1 with a bounded source atom — the IP value is NEVER tagged (GDPR + cardinality). MEANS: on a Fly deploy this should be dominated by trusted_proxy; remote_ip is expected only for local/dev/ExUnit traffic. WATCH: unexpected remote_ip on a Fly deploy means the fly-client-ip edge header isn't arriving and requests are bypassing the trusted-proxy keying — a rate-limit bypass / mis-attribution risk.

panels.title: Event pipeline throughput (emitted · invoked · errors)
panels.description: WHAT: the three flow rates of the Oban-backed event bus — events appended to op.event_log (emitted), handler invocations (invoked), and handler errors (errors). HOW: rate over stacks_events_emitted_count_total, stacks_events_handler_invoked_count_total and stacks_events_handler_error_count_total (the last fires on a returned {:error, _} OR a raise). MEANS: emitted and invoked track together (fan-out to subscribers); errors should sit at or near ZERO. WATCH: handler_error climbing is the failure signal — a subscriber is failing (enrichment / cache / dbt-refresh not running); invoked collapsing to zero while emitted continues means dispatch is stalled (SubscriberWorker backed up or the:events queue paused).

panels.title: Handler dispatch duration p95
panels.description: WHAT: 95th-percentile wall-clock time for one SubscriberWorker handle_event/1 call. HOW: histogram_quantile(0.95) over the rate of stacks_events_dispatch_duration_milliseconds_bucket (the _bucket series of the dispatch distribution). MEANS: most handlers are DB-only and finish in tens of ms, so a healthy p95 sits low; the value is in milliseconds. WATCH: a rising p95 flags a slow handler (typically one making an external HTTP call — enrichment/scraper/vision) that is holding the:events queue; correlate with the handler-error panel and the repo-query p95 to tell a slow subscriber apart from slow DB.

panels.title: Circuit-breaker state by fuse
panels.description: WHAT: the current up/down state of each Fuse circuit breaker (vision / scraper / Brave etc.), one lane per fuse_name. HOW: the last_value gauge stacks_fuse_state_state, where 1 = healthy (closed, calls flowing) and 0 = blown (open, calls short-circuited). This is a GAUGE — read the raw value, do NOT rate it. MEANS: all lanes should read 1 in steady state; a lane dropping to 0 shows exactly which external dependency is currently tripped and being bypassed. WATCH: a fuse stuck at 0 means that dependency is failing enough to keep the breaker open (investigate that upstream); flapping 0/1 means it is recovering intermittently and the melt threshold or timeout may need tuning.

panels.title: Repo-query duration p95
panels.description: WHAT: 95th-percentile duration of a single PostgreSQL round-trip. HOW: histogram_quantile(0.95) over the rate of stacks_repo_query_duration_milliseconds_bucket (emitted per Ecto query, tagged by worker/source/repo). MEANS: most queries are <50ms so a healthy p95 is low; the value is in milliseconds and is the raw DB-health SLI. WATCH: a rising p95 means the database is the bottleneck — a missing index, a heavy Oban worker saturating Core.Repo's pool, or connection-pool queueing; cross-check with the router-dispatch p95 to separate slow DB from slow endpoint code.

panels.title: Router-dispatch duration p95
panels.description: WHAT: 95th-percentile Phoenix route-dispatch latency (controller action wall-time), broken down by route group. HOW: histogram_quantile(0.95) over the rate of stacks_router_dispatch_stop_duration_milliseconds_bucket, tagged by route_group (auth / catalogue / upload / …). MEANS: this is the user-facing endpoint-latency SLI in milliseconds; each route group carries its own p95 target (auth/catalogue ~500ms, upload ~2000ms). WATCH: a route group breaching its target is a regression or downstream stall for that surface; if router p95 rises together with repo-query p95 the cause is the DB, if router rises alone the cause is in the endpoint/handler code.

panels.title: Upload terminal outcomes
panels.description: WHAT: rate of upload-pipeline jobs reaching a terminal state, split by outcome (resolved / rejected / timeout). HOW: rate over stacks_upload_terminal_count_total, emitted once per job when the vision→ISBN pipeline finishes. MEANS: a healthy pipeline is dominated by resolved with a modest rejected background (not-a-book / no-ISBN uploads); the value is jobs-per-second by outcome. WATCH: a rejected surge means users are uploading non-book / unresolvable images (or the vision/ISBN resolver regressed); a timeout surge means the Modal vision calls or the resolver are stalling — cross-check the fuse-state panel for a tripped vision/scraper breaker.

panels.title: Vision call latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: WHAT: wall-clock time for ONE Modal vision HTTP call (classify / extract / analyze / associate), at the 50th, 95th and 99th percentile. HOW: histogram_quantile over the rate of stacks_vision_request_stop_duration_milliseconds_bucket, emitted by Stacks.AI.Client on every call that got an HTTP response — success or not. MEANS: the value is milliseconds per call, and an upload makes up to two of these back to back, so the upload's own latency floor is roughly twice p50; the long-standing '~3–8s per upload' figure was an estimate in a comment, and the first real measurement put p50 at 8.4s with warm calls under 30s and cold starts under 60s. READ IT WITH THE PANEL BESIDE IT: these quantiles only count calls that got a response, so a call that hits the client's 330s deadline is absent from this panel entirely and appears only as a vision give-up. WATCH: p99 climbing past the 60s (cold-start) edge means something other than a cold start is slow — most likely uploads queuing on a single A10G, the term Modal's own 300s timeout was sized for; a p50 that jumps while p99 is flat is a container-warmth shift, and both quantiles rising together with the upload-terminal timeout count is the vision backend degrading.

panels.title: Vision give-ups by failure class
panels.description: WHAT: rate of Modal vision calls that produced no HTTP response at all, split by the bounded reason the socket layer gave. HOW: rate over stacks_vision_request_exception_count_total, emitted by Stacks.AI.Client whenever Finch returns an error instead of a response. MEANS: these calls are INVISIBLE on the latency panel beside this one — a call that never answers emits no duration — so this is the only place the client's own deadline shows up, and the GPU work behind a give-up keeps running and keeps billing while nobody reads the result. WATCH: reason_class=timeout going non-zero is the important one: the client waits 330s and Modal's own function timeout is 300s, so a timeout here means Modal exceeded its own deadline and the derived Stacks.AI.Client.receive_timeout_ms/0 needs revisiting — note these are classified transient and therefore RETRIED, so each one costs three cold starts on a contended GPU. reason_class=pool_timeout is the opposite problem and is local: Finch ran out of connections and never reached Modal. unreachable/closed point at the sidecar being down or redeploying — cross-check the fuse-state panel for a blown vision breaker.

panels.title: Database reachable
panels.description: WHAT: whether the app's last database ping succeeded — 1 (OK) means the watchdog's SELECT 1 worked, 0 (DOWN) means the database is refusing us (outage, exhausted free-tier compute quota, bad credentials). HOW: last known value of stacks_fuse_state_state{fuse_name="neon_fuse"} within 2h; the watchdog melts the fuse on ping failure so this reads 0 within ~1 minute of an outage even with zero user traffic. MEANS: DOWN here with green app health checks is precisely the failure mode that hid the quota outage — the app was up, the database was not. WATCH: 'No data' means the app itself has been asleep for 2h+ (scale-to-zero) — the database state is UNKNOWN, not healthy; wake the app or check Neon directly.
